criterion: The user chooses the action being tracked.
rationale: Agency starts with a goal selected by the person, not inferred by the product.
evidence_prompt: Show where a user creates or selects the action.

criterion: The action can be described in observable terms.
rationale: Observable actions are easier to review than vague promises about identity or health.
evidence_prompt: Record the goal label, schedule and completion rule.

criterion: A goal can be edited, paused or removed.
rationale: Changing circumstances should not trap a person in an obsolete commitment.
evidence_prompt: Demonstrate the edit, pause and deletion controls.

criterion: The interface distinguishes user input from calculated progress.
rationale: People should know which facts they entered and which values the product derived.
evidence_prompt: Label a completion, a calculated count and any inferred status.

criterion: Decorative rewards are identifiable as product mechanics.
rationale: Animation and collectibles can motivate without being presented as scientific evidence.
evidence_prompt: Identify each decorative reward and the action that unlocks it.

criterion: Streak and completion calculations are explainable.
rationale: A visible calculation lets users understand resets, time zones and missed entries.
evidence_prompt: Document the calculation, reset rule and time-zone behavior.

criterion: A missed day has a clear return path.
rationale: Recovery supports continued use without turning one lapse into a disproportionate penalty.
evidence_prompt: Demonstrate the first session after a missed day.

criterion: Copy avoids shame, diagnosis and moral judgment.
rationale: A tracker should report product state without judging the person.
evidence_prompt: Review empty, lapse, reminder and cancellation messages.

criterion: Historical progress remains understandable after a break.
rationale: People need an accurate record even when continuity changes.
evidence_prompt: Inspect how gaps and prior completions are displayed.

criterion: Reminders are optional and controllable.
rationale: Notifications should support a chosen routine, not manufacture urgency.
evidence_prompt: Show opt-in, schedule, mute and disable controls.

criterion: The product works without manipulative countdowns or false scarcity.
rationale: Artificial urgency can displace the user’s goal with the product’s engagement target.
evidence_prompt: Review purchase, streak and reward prompts for time pressure.

criterion: Reduced-motion and interruption needs are considered.
rationale: Visual reward systems should remain usable when motion or repeated interruption is unwelcome.
evidence_prompt: Test system motion settings and notification-disabled use.

criterion: Social participation is optional.
rationale: Private self-tracking should not require public performance.
evidence_prompt: Complete the core workflow without adding contacts or posting.

criterion: Audience and visibility are clear before sharing.
rationale: Users need to know who can see a goal, completion or media item.
evidence_prompt: Capture the audience selector and resulting view.

criterion: Rankings and comparison do not redefine personal progress.
rationale: Competitive mechanics can create pressure unrelated to the chosen action.
evidence_prompt: Document whether leaderboards exist and how they can be avoided.

criterion: Collected data is described at the point it matters.
rationale: A plain-language explanation supports informed use and later review.
evidence_prompt: Map each core screen to the relevant privacy disclosure.

criterion: Deletion and account exit are discoverable.
rationale: A user should be able to leave without an opaque support maze.
evidence_prompt: Test the public and in-product deletion path.

criterion: Feature claims are separated from outcome claims.
rationale: A working feature does not by itself prove behavior change or health benefit.
evidence_prompt: Classify every material claim as feature, hypothesis or measured outcome.

criterion: Any outcome report states context, measures and limitations.
rationale: Without those details, a testimonial or metric cannot support a general conclusion.
evidence_prompt: Check the app version, period, sample, measure, attrition and comparison.

criterion: Medical or psychological claims have appropriate evidence and review.
rationale: Habit software should not imply treatment, diagnosis or guaranteed benefit without support.
evidence_prompt: List health-related wording and the evidence and review behind it.
